newsitem.title: USA: Union calls for boycott on eve of talks with Crown.
newsitem.headline: Union calls for boycott on eve of talks with Crown.

text.p: Union workers locked out of a Crown Central Petroleum Corp. refinery called Thursday for a boycott of the company's gasoline stations on the eve of a new round of talks on a labour contract.

Members of the Oil, Chemical and Atomic Workers Local 4-227, which represents 225 workers at Crown's refinery in Pasadena, Texas, said there has been no progress in talks aimed at settling the 10-month lock out.
"We are calling for a nationwide boycott of Crown, and this has been endorsed by the national AFL-CIO," said Joe Campbell, secretary-treasurer of the union local.

A federal mediator called both sides to a meeting on Friday to restart talks stalled over terms of a new labour pact that would allow the company to replace 40 percent of its union workers with contractors at the refinery.
"We've been trying to get them to talk for a long time," Crown spokesman Joe Coale said. "(The boycott) is just part of their strategy to keep the pressure on."

The union workers were locked out on February 5 after the company said some equipment at the refinery was vandalised. A local National Labour Relations Board administrative judge later dismissed an unfair labour practices claim filed by the union, and a decision on the union's appeal is pending.
During the lock-out, union workers complained the company has blocked access to their 401(k) retirement accounts, which some workers sought to make mortgage and tuition payments.
Several longtime refinery workers also have made personal appeals to Crown Chairman Henry Rosenberg to step in and resolve the dispute.
Campbell said workers were blocked from the company's annual meeting. "In our opinion, it's just a move on their part to bust the union," Campbell said.

Union officials today stepped up their attack on a company they said has made a series of missteps, and a longtime dealer said he joined the union's calls for a boycott after Crown refused to renew leases on two stations in Baltimore.
"It appears that Crown is trying to squeeze us both to compensate for their gross mismanagement," station owner Brian Porter said.
